thread:
emma_cust: Hey team — after we moved traffic to PrivateLink endpoints, our app is seeing intermittent 502s and huge tail latency when talking to Redwood API. Started after cutover at ~09:00 UTC.

maria_support: Sorry you're hitting that — can you paste the failing curl and any error IDs? Is this hosted or dedicated?

emma_cust: Hosted (using redwood.prod.mycorp). Error we get in app: "502 read ECONNRESET from upstream". No error id from Redwood side in the body. Sample curl that reproduces: 

```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \ \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \
  --resolve api.redwood.example:443:10.2.5.11 \
  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```

maria_support: OK thanks. Can you also run a traceroute/tcpdump from the app host and share route table for the subnets and the VPC endpoint ENIs?

sam_sre: looping in neteng — my initial hunch: asymmetric routing or TLS inspection by customer's network firewall causing SNI mismatch -> backend rejects.

jin_neteng: @sam_sre quick checklist: 1) is VPCE interface in same AZ as instance? 2) route table has local route to endpoint ENI IPs? 3) SG on vpce allows inbound from app subnet? 4) any transparent proxy / TLS inspect?

emma_cust: Traces attached (pasted outputs). Traceroute shows hops to 10.2.5.11 then goes out to NAT and back via IGW sometimes. Route table: main RT has 10.2.0.0/16 local, 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-abcde. No explicit route for vpce-eni IPs. Security group on VPCE is default allow HTTPS from 10.2.0.0/16. We do run AWS Network Firewall in the TGW egress path and have TLS inspection enabled for outbound https.

sam_sre: That NAT->IGW return path is suspicious. Interface endpoints require the instance traffic to reach the ENI directly; if replies return via NAT/IGW you get asymmetric routing and the endpoint or NLB will drop/close. Can you run tcpdump on the instance while reproducing? Look for TLS ClientHello destination IP and SNI.

emma_cust: tcpdump snippet: 

```
12:15:01.123456 IP 10.2.10.45.52344 > 10.2.5.11.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240
12:15:01.223789 IP firewall-gw > 10.2.10.45.52344: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0
```

And openssl s_client output when forcing the endpoint IP: 

```
openssl s_client -connect 10.2.5.11:443 -servername api.redwood.example
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = *.othercorp.com
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
no peer cert available
---
```

maria_support: Aha — certificate CN is for othercorp.com. That indicates the Network Firewall/TLS inspector is intercepting and presenting its own cert (TLS MITM) or traffic is being forwarded to a proxy that rewrites SNI. Both will break mutual TLS expectations and can cause upstream to reset.

jin_neteng: Confirmed: firewall doing TLS inspection -> replaces SNI with original host? It may also route traffic out to internet proxy which then hits Redwood public ingress, causing mismatch with PrivateLink NLB target certificate. PrivateLink is expecting SNI for the internal service name and a direct ENI path. If your egress path routes to NAT/IGW, you hit the public endpoint and cert doesn't match.

sam_sre: Repro steps we used:
1) from app host: curl --resolve api.redwood.example:443:10.2.5.11 -I https://api.redwood.example/status  (works when path is direct)
2) enable firewall TLS inspect -> curl returns 502/connection reset and the presented cert CN is firewall appliance.
3) traceroute shows next-hop to nat-xxx instead of ENI for some flows due to missing VPC endpoint route policy on a custom route table.

jin_neteng: Root causes identified (multiple):
- Missing route propagation / explicit route for VPCE ENI subnet in some private route tables -> asymmetric routing via NAT.
- TLS inspection in TGW/NAT path causing cert rewrite and SNI mismatch.
- Network Firewall policy denies or rewrites healthcheck probes intermittently resulting in NLB target marked unhealthy -> 502s and high tail latency.

maria_support: Action plan for customer (quick wins):
- Add explicit route entries in affected route tables so traffic to VPCE ENI IPs stays local (avoid NAT/IGW). Example: `10.2.5.11/32 -> local` or ensure the VPC route for endpoint ENIs is present.
- Add firewall exception for api.redwood.example (or for the VPCE subnet) to bypass TLS inspection for Redwood egress. If bypass not possible, configure TLS inspection to preserve SNI and not rewrite certs for this destination.
- Verify security group on endpoint allows health checks from NLB (if applicable) and that endpoint is in same AZ as app subnets.
- Temporarily whitelist Redwood public IPs in allowlist for auth callbacks while cutover completes (if you use IP allowlist at upstream).

jin_neteng: Commands we recommended they run:
```
# list VPCE ENI IPs
aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=description,Values="*vpce*" --query 'NetworkInterfaces[*].PrivateIpAddress'
# verify route table entries
aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-xxxx --query 'RouteTables[*].Routes'
# tcpdump reproduction
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.2.5.11 and port 443 -w /tmp/trace.pcap
# validate cert presented
openssl s_client -connect 10.2.5.11:443 -servername api.redwood.example -showcerts
```

emma_cust: We added explicit /32 routes to the endpoint ENIs into the app subnet route tables and created a firewall bypass rule for api.redwood.example. After that latency dropped and 502s stopped. Confirmed with curl and app smoke tests.

maria_support: Awesome — glad that worked. Two follow-ups: 1) we'll add a KB article explaining common VPCE asymmetry + TLS-inspect gotchas for PrivateLink customers, and 2) please paste the NAT/RT config and firewall rule IDs so we can keep a sanitized copy with support ticket INC-984321.

emma_cust: Pasted sanitized configs in ticket. Thanks for quick triage, team! :tada:

deploy-bot: Removed SLO alert for api.redwood.example in us-east-1 (alert 6789) — condition recovered at 12:17:10 UTC.

sam_sre: marking this as resolved from our side. I'll follow up with the docs PR and request that product include a short PrivateLink checklist in onboarding.
